data.reason: I decide for the regulation officer. Proposal 1 is strong for customers: on-time 216.6 → 223.8 (+7.2, 5/5 seeds), late 11.4 → 4.2, lowest on-time rate 0.93 → 0.97. But R1 does not approve proposal 1 alone. It permanently lets any single company pass any rule change that clears check, the invariants and a same-seed improvement in on_time_deliveries. That improvement test does not guard road safety or the other companies' utility. Proposal 1 itself shows the risk. Road violations rise 19.0 → 28.0, about 47% more, which affects everyone who shares the roads. C's utility falls 65.8 → 56.3 and B's falls 68.5 → 65.5, while only A gains (69.8 → 73.4). Under quorum 1, B and C would lose their protection against such changes in every later period, not just this one. I depart from the LLM's recommendation of R1. A one-off customer gain of about 7 on-time deliveries per period does not justify removing a lasting check from the voting process. It would also set a precedent that harmed companies cannot block rule changes. The cost to customers is real: about 7 more late deliveries per period, and the weakest company's customers stay at 0.93. A narrower instrument, such as a safeguard-based quorum or an invariant limiting road violations, would deserve consideration, but none was measured. Keeping v1 matches the vote result A ○, B ×, C ×. This settles D1.f1: the regulator does not revise the quorum rule and approves no override for block_k 3 → 2.
assumptions: Next period's conditions resemble this period's, so proposal 1's measured gain and costs are representative.
